title: In Exodus 31 In What Ways Can We Apply The Principles Of Teamwork And Collaboration Seen In The Calling Of Bezalel And Oholiab To Our Own Ministries
paragraphs: The Calling of Bezalel and Oholiab: A Model for Teamwork in Ministry

The story of Bezalel and Oholiab in Exodus 31 offers a powerful biblical example of God-ordained teamwork and collaboration. As the Israelites journeyed through the wilderness, God gave Moses specific instructions for the construction of the Tabernacle—a dwelling place for His presence among His people. To accomplish this monumental task, God did not appoint Moses alone, but called and equipped skilled individuals to work together in unity and purpose.
God’s Initiative in Appointing and Empowering
The passage begins with God identifying Bezalel by name, filling him with the Spirit of God, and granting him wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and craftsmanship:

See, I have called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah: and I have filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship. - Exodus 31:2-3 ASV

God also appointed Oholiab and gifted others with skills to assist in the work (Exodus 31:6 ASV). This shows that ministry is not a solo endeavor, but a cooperative one, initiated and empowered by God Himself.
Principles of Teamwork and Collaboration for Ministry
1. Recognizing Diverse Gifts and Callings
God called Bezalel and Oholiab for specific roles. In ministry today, not everyone has the same gifts, but all are essential. The New Testament echoes this principle:
But now hath God set the members each one of them in the body, even as it pleased him. - 1 Corinthians 12:18 ASV
Application: Identify and affirm the unique gifts in your church or ministry. Encourage each member to serve according to their God-given abilities.
2. Spirit-Empowered Service
Bezalel was filled with the Spirit for his task. True teamwork requires more than talent; it relies on the Holy Spirit’s empowerment.
Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, saith Jehovah of hosts. - Zechariah 4:6 ASV
Application: Pray for the Spirit’s guidance and strength as you work together. Seek unity that comes from relying on God, not just human effort.
3. Valuing Every Contribution
The Tabernacle required many kinds of workmanship—artistry, weaving, metalwork, and more. Each contribution was valuable for the completion of God’s sanctuary.

From whom all the body fitly framed and knit together through that which every joint supplieth, according to the working in due measure of each several part, maketh the increase of the body unto the building up of itself in love. - Ephesians 4:16 ASV
Application: Foster an environment where every role is honored—from visible leadership to behind-the-scenes service.
4. Obedience to God’s Blueprint
Bezalel and Oholiab followed precise instructions given by God through Moses. Effective ministry collaboration means working together under God’s direction, not our own agendas.
And Moses did according to all that Jehovah commanded him, so did he. - Exodus 40:16 ASV
Application: Base your strategies and plans on God’s Word and direction, seeking His will above personal preferences.
Christ-Centered Teamwork
The Tabernacle pointed forward to Christ, the ultimate meeting place between God and humanity (John 1:14 ASV). Our teamwork should reflect His love, humility, and sacrificial service:
For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many. - Mark 10:45 ASV
Conclusion: Building Together for God’s Glory

The collaboration of Bezalel, Oholiab, and the skilled workers reminds us that God’s work is best accomplished when His people unite, empowered by the Spirit, honoring each other’s gifts, and submitting to His will. In our own ministries, let us strive for this biblical model of teamwork—so that Christ is glorified, and His Kingdom advances.
